DeclaredFigure.description:
One number a section is allowed to state, and where it came from.

`rendered` is the exact string the prose uses, so the check that follows compares like with
like; `source` names the field on the scoring run it was read from, so a reader (or GRS-0222)
can trace any number in the report back to the run that produced it.

key.description: Stable identifier, unique within the section.
key.title: Key

label.description: What this figure is, in the reader's words.
label.title: Label

rendered.description: Exactly as it appears in the prose, e.g. '£1.2m' or '61'.
rendered.title: Rendered

source.description: Where it came from on the scoring run, e.g. 'run.platform_value.point'.
source.title: Source

DeclaredFigure.title: DeclaredFigure

ReportSectionKind.description:
The sections of a client report, in the order they are read.

The body opens with the business and closes with what acting is worth; the appendix carries
every number the body refers to. `SECTION_ORDER` below is normative.
ReportSectionKind.title: ReportSectionKind

ReportTier.description:
Which audience a section is cleared for (the hook GRS-0214 will decide against).

Declared per section so tiering is a property of the content, not of a renderer's filter.
ReportTier.title: ReportTier

description: One section of the report: prose, the figures that prose is allowed to cite, and its gate.

ai_drafted.description: Whether the prose began as an AI draft. If so it needs an approved narrative.
ai_drafted.title: Ai Drafted

body.description: Paragraphs of plain prose. No markup — the renditions own presentation.
body.title: Body

narrative_id.description: The approved AINarrative this prose came from. Required when ai_drafted.
narrative_id.title: Narrative Id
